148	### 2.4 Wire and CN: the exact count rides on the RPC that already reads the footers
149	
150	Proto (`internal_service.proto:647-650`, new patch file `patches/files-schema-row-count-proto.patch`):
151	
152	```proto
153	message PGetFileSchemaResult {
154	    required StatusPB status = 1;
155	    repeated PSlotDescriptor schema = 2;
156	    // Sirius extension: exact row total over every range in the request, from the parquet footers the node
157	    // opened for the schema. Absent when the node cannot count (upstream BE samples files and does not set it).
158	    optional int64 num_rows = 3;
159	};
160	```
161	
162	proto2 `optional` on an existing message is wire-compatible in both directions: a stock FE ignores the field, a
163	stock BE never sets it, the FE falls back (2.1).
164	
165	CN (`file_schema.rs`): `parquet_file_schema` returns `(Vec<PSlotDescriptor>, i64)` with
166	`builder.metadata().file_metadata().num_rows()`; `parquet_files_schema` (:62-95) sums the per-file counts while it
167	runs its existing name/type agreement loop and returns a small struct:
168	
169	```rust
170	pub(crate) struct FilesSchema { pub slots: Vec<PSlotDescriptor>, pub num_rows: i64 }
171	```
172	
173	Handler (`compute_node_service.rs:681-699`): `PGetFileSchemaResult { status, schema: s.slots, num_rows: Some(s.num_rows) }`
174	on success, `num_rows: None` on error. `file_schema_from_attachment` (:1683-1707) is unchanged apart from the return
175	type.
176	
177	Cost: zero extra I/O. The CN deliberately reads every footer already (`file_schema.rs:59-61`: whole-set agreement is
178	the contract; P4 measured the lineitem call at 28.3 ms busy for 60 footers). Interaction with P4's proposed fix
179	(section 4 item 7 of the report): that fix must stay "concurrent + memoised", not "sample N files", or the total
180	becomes partial; the design defines `num_rows` as exact-or-absent, so a sampling CN must send `None`.
181	
182	`build.rs` guard (:72-108, `require_exchange_proto_patch`): add a second `(token, patch)` pair,
183	`("num_rows = 3", "patches/files-schema-row-count-proto.patch")`, so a checkout missing the patch fails with the
184	one-line fix instead of `no field num_rows on PGetFileSchemaResult` 200 lines later (the guard's stated purpose).

280	### 4.2 The six 1-CN failures: the FE will still shuffle lineitem (inference, computed from the cost code)
281	
282	q05's lineitem join at 1 CN with exact counts. L = lineitem projection 6e9 rows x 28 B = 168 GB (measured parked
283	projection at death 171 GB, P1); R = customer x orders(0.25) = 3.75e8 rows x 12 B = 4.5 GB. `getRealCost`
284	weights 0.5/2/1.5 (`CostModel.java:129-135`):
285	
286	| term | BROADCAST R | SHUFFLE both |
287	|---|---:|---:|
288	| exchange (`visitPhysicalDistribution` :400-460; CN-only so `aliveBackendNumber = 0`, beNum 1; single registered node so shuffle network cost 0, `SystemInfoService.isSingleBackendAndComputeNode` :246-248) | 2R + 1.5R = 15.8, x1000 because 4.5 GB > `exec_mem_limit` 2 GiB (:426-428, `SessionVariable.DEFAULT_EXEC_MEM_LIMIT` :1305) = 15,750 | 0.5(L+R) = 86 |
289	| hash join (`HashJoinCostModel.getCpuCost/getMemCost/getAvgProbeCost` :85-157) | probe penalty min(12, ln(3.75e8/1e5)) = 8.2 -> 0.5(R + 8.2L) + 2R = 703 | penalty min(3, 8.2 - log2(parallelFactor)) = 3 -> 0.5(R + 3L) + 2R = 263 |
290	| total | 16,453 (718 even with the memory penalty removed) | 350 |
291	
292	SHUFFLE wins by 2x even with `exec_mem_limit` raised; broadcast wins at 1 CN only while ln(R_rows/1e5) < ~4, i.e.
293	build sides under ~5.5M rows (nation, region, supplier, filtered part). Each of the six has a lineitem join whose
294	other side is orders- or partsupp-derived (1e8-1e9 rows), so all six keep the P1 shape at 1 CN. With 4 registered
295	nodes (the survey condition, P3) shuffle network cost is nonzero and the margin narrows (345 vs 718 for the
296	exchanges) but the join penalty term still decides for shuffle. **Conclusion: fix 3 does not un-break the six; fix
297	4 does.** Fix 1 (fail fast) is what makes the still-wrong plans cheap to observe.

360	## 7. Risks (ranked) and mitigations
361	
362	1. **RIGHT SEMI plans hit a translator gap (high likelihood, high impact).** `JoinCommutativityRule` maps
363	   LEFT_SEMI <-> RIGHT_SEMI (:34-44); `node_translator.rs:1743-1762` has no `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN` arm ("hash join type is
364	   unsupported"). q04, q18, q20, q21 carry LEFT SEMI joins whose other side is now estimated smaller. Mitigation:
365	   land plan item 5 (translator `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN => (RightSemi, JoinOutput::Right)`; the Substrait consumer and
366	   engine already support it, P5) **before** enabling the Config by default in the bench; until then run with the
367	   Config off. RIGHT_ANTI is already translated (:1750), so q22's commutation is safe.
368	2. **CTE reuse turns on and the CN refuses `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` (high likelihood for q15/q11, high
369	   impact).** Cost arithmetic in 4.3. Mitigation: acceptance runs `SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse = false` (existing
370	   session variable, `SessionVariable.java:499/1506`, wired at `OptimizerContext.java:98`), which reproduces today's
371	   inline plans exactly; documented in the TUNABLES row; lifted when plan item 9 lands. This is also the fix for the
372	   q15 double scan, so the two fixes are complementary, not competing.
373	3. **1-CN broadcast-to-shuffle flips park a large probe (medium likelihood, high impact).** With real counts the
374	   guard rejects q03's orders x customer broadcast (72 GB < 120 GB), so lineitem (78 GB measured on cn4, summed)
375	   would be parked at 1 CN in a 100 GiB pool with 58-80% cold-start reservations (C3): q03 goes from 3.1 s to
376	   marginal or OOM. Same mechanism, smaller volumes, for q12 (orders 36 GB) and q10. Mitigations, in order: (i)
377	   `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 CN before any sweep; (ii) GPU-sized `broadcast_row_limit` (session, no code) for the 1-CN
378	   arm and a documented row; (iii) fix 4a (fusion) removes the exchange at 1 CN entirely and makes this moot; (iv)
379	   fix 1 makes a bad case cost seconds.
380	4. **Fallback estimator error (0.2-6x) inverts partsupp/orders and part/customer** (measured table 4.1). Only in
381	   fallback mode (no CN `num_rows`); the exact path removes it. The FE UT covers the fallback with `fake://`.
382	5. **Patch drift on submodule bumps.** Three Java files plus the proto; `apply-starrocks-patches.sh` fails loudly
383	   (`exit 1`). The Java change is small and plausibly upstreamable to StarRocks (it is the Hive rule applied to
384	   FILES()), which would shrink the patch over time.
385	6. **Load path shares the operator.** `INSERT ... SELECT FROM FILES()` gets the same estimate; harmless for
386	   correctness, may change load plan text. Existing FE UTs that plan `fake://` FILES() (`PipeManagerTest`,
387	   `StatementPlannerTest`) assert structure, not `cardinality:` lines (checked by grep), so none should break.
388	7. **Determinism.** Statistics are a pure function of file sizes/footers; plans are stable across runs. The fallback
389	   depends on compression (a different copy of the same table gives different estimates); the exact path does not.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-applies Sirius-only patches onto the vendored StarRocks checkout.
# Safe to re-run: skips a patch that already applies (or is already present).
set -euo pipefail

root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
submodule="$root/starrocks"
patch_dir="$root/patches"

if [[ ! -f "$submodule/gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto" ]]; then
  echo "StarRocks submodule is not checked out at $submodule" >&2
  echo "Run: git submodule update --init --recursive experimental/starrocks/starrocks" >&2
  exit 1
fi

shopt -s nullglob
patches=("$patch_dir"/*.patch)
if ((${#patches[@]} == 0)); then
  echo "No patches under $patch_dir" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$submodule"
for patch in "${patches[@]}"; do
  if git apply --check "$patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git apply "$patch"
    echo "applied $(basename "$patch")"
  elif git apply --reverse --check "$patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "already applied $(basename "$patch")"
  else
    echo "failed to apply $(basename "$patch")" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Translate-only survey of all 22 TPC-H queries on the SF1000 paths with ONE CN (SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY=1): the CN accepts and
# translates every fragment without executing it, so each query only costs an FE plan + translation; the client times out.
# Also captures EXPLAIN COSTS and EXPLAIN VERBOSE per query (FE-side plans and cardinality estimates).
SP=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad
WT=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf; OUT=$SP/perf/sf1000/survey; DATA=/scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000
QD=$WT/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT/explain $OUT/dump; rm -f $OUT/dump/*
source $SP/cluster-env.sh $WT
export NUM_CNS=1 GPU_MEM=64GiB HOST_MEM=128GiB STAGING=8GiB SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY=1 SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS=$OUT/dump
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
echo "##### SURVEY start $(date -u +%T)"
bash $SP/start-cluster.sh $WT $OUT/cluster.log
for i in $(seq 1 60); do n=$($M -e "SHOW COMPUTE NODES;" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="Alive") c=i; next} $c=="true"{n++} END{print n+0}'); [ "$n" = "1" ] && break; sleep 3; done
echo "alive=$n after $((i*3))s"
for q in $(seq -f 'q%02g' 1 22); do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  $M -e "EXPLAIN COSTS $sql" > $OUT/explain/$q.costs.txt 2>&1
  $M -e "EXPLAIN VERBOSE $sql" > $OUT/explain/$q.verbose.txt 2>&1
  before=$(wc -l < $OUT/cluster.log)
  timeout 20 $M -e "/* survey $q */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.out 2> $OUT/$q.err; rc=$?
  sleep 1
  tail -n +$((before+1)) $OUT/cluster.log | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -a -iE 'translate|unsupported|error|fragment' | grep -av 'AuditLog\|INFO (' > $OUT/$q.cnlog
  nt=$(grep -c 'accepting untranslatable' $OUT/$q.cnlog); ok=$(grep -c -iE 'translated fragment|translate_fragment_logged.*close' $OUT/$q.cnlog)
  fe_err=$(head -c 200 $OUT/$q.err | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "$q rc=$rc untranslatable_fragments=$nt translate_events=$ok explain_costs_lines=$(wc -l < $OUT/explain/$q.costs.txt) fe_err=${fe_err:0:120}"
done
echo "##### stopping $(date -u +%T)"; bash $SP/stop-cluster.sh $WT
echo "##### SURVEY DONE $(date -u +%T)"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarize StarRocks EXPLAIN COSTS output: fragments, joins (op, distribution, conjunct, probe/build children),
aggregations, exchanges, cardinality estimates. usage: explain_summary.py <costs.txt> [...]"""
import re, sys, os, json
def parse(path):
    t = open(path).read(); lines = t.splitlines()
    frags = re.findall(r'^PLAN FRAGMENT (\d+)\(F(\d+)\)', t, re.M)
    cards = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'cardinality:\s*(\d+)', t)]
    # node lines: indentation + "N:NAME"
    nodes = []
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^(\s*)(\|----)?(\d+):([A-Z][A-Z \-]+?)(?:\s*\(.*\))?\s*$', l)
        if m: nodes.append((i, len(m.group(1)) + (5 if m.group(2) else 0), int(m.group(3)), m.group(4).strip(), bool(m.group(2))))
    # fragment -> output exchange id and scanned tables (by column prefix under FileScanNode)
    PFX = {'l_':'lineitem','o_':'orders','c_':'customer','p_':'part','ps_':'partsupp','s_':'supplier','n_':'nation','r_':'region'}
    frag_blocks = re.split(r'^PLAN FRAGMENT ', t, flags=re.M)[1:]
    exch_src = {}   # exchange id -> tables produced by the fragment that outputs it
    frag_tables = {}
    for fb in frag_blocks:
        fid = re.match(r'(\d+)', fb).group(1)
        m = re.search(r'OutPut Exchange Id: (\d+)', fb)
        tabs = set()
        for scan in re.finditer(r'\d+:FileScanNode\n((?:.*\n){1,40}?)(?=\n\s*\n|\d+:|PLAN FRAGMENT|\Z)', fb):
            for col in re.findall(r'\* (ps_|l_|o_|c_|p_|s_|n_|r_)', scan.group(1)): tabs.add(PFX[col])
        # exchanges consumed inside this fragment carry their sources too
        for eid in re.findall(r'(\d+):(?:MERGING-)?EXCHANGE', fb): tabs |= set(exch_src.get(eid, set()))
        frag_tables[fid] = tabs
        if m: exch_src[str(int(m.group(1)))] = tabs
    joins = []
    for idx, (i, ind, nid, name, right) in enumerate(nodes):
        if 'JOIN' not in name: continue
        body = '\n'.join(lines[i+1:i+40])
        op = re.search(r'join op: ([^\n]+)', body); conj = re.findall(r'equal join conjunct: ([^\n]+)', body)
        later = nodes[idx+1:]
        rk = next((n for n in later if n[4] and n[1] > ind), None)
        # probe child: first later node at the join's own indentation that is not a build child
        pk = next((n for n in later if not n[4] and n[1] == ind), None)
        def desc(n):
            if n is None: return '?'
            src = ''
            if 'EXCHANGE' in n[3]:
                src = '<-' + '+'.join(sorted(exch_src.get(str(n[2]), []))) if exch_src.get(str(n[2])) else ''
            return f"{n[2]}:{n[3]}{src}"
        joins.append({'node': nid, 'op': op.group(1).strip() if op else name, 'conjuncts': [c.strip() for c in conj],
                      'probe_child': desc(pk), 'build_child': desc(rk)})
    aggs = re.findall(r'(\d+):AGGREGATE \(([a-z ]+)\)', t)
    exch = re.findall(r'(\d+):(?:MERGING-)?EXCHANGE\n\s*distribution type: ([A-Z_]+)', t)
    scans = re.findall(r'(\d+):FileScanNode', t)
    tables = re.findall(r'file://[^/]*/[^/]*/[^/]*/[^/]*/([a-z]+)/\*', t)  # weak; FILES path may not appear in COSTS
    topn = re.findall(r'(\d+):TOP-N', t)
    return {'query': os.path.basename(path).split('.')[0], 'fragments': len(frags), 'nodes': len(nodes), 'scans': len(scans),
            'joins': joins, 'aggs': [f"{n}:{p}" for n, p in aggs], 'exchanges': [f"{n}:{d}" for n, d in exch], 'topn': topn,
            'cardinalities': {'n': len(cards), 'all_one': all(c == 1 for c in cards), 'max': max(cards) if cards else None}}
if __name__ == '__main__':
    out = [parse(p) for p in sys.argv[1:]]
    if len(out) == 1: print(json.dumps(out[0], indent=1)); sys.exit()
    for o in out:
        js = '; '.join(f"{j['node']}:{j['op']} build={j['build_child']} probe={j['probe_child']}" for j in o['joins'])
        print(f"{o['query']} frags={o['fragments']} scans={o['scans']} card_all_one={o['cardinalities']['all_one']} aggs={','.join(o['aggs'])} exch={','.join(o['exchanges'])}\n    joins: {js}")

content.content:
### 3C. Backpressure

#### B1 (confirmed). Receiver-first rendezvous plus one fragment at a time turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation

**Source (verified).** `engine.rs:278-280`: `// One request at a time until the handle (and its sender) is dropped` `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`; `run_fragment_inner` (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> `build()` -> `relay_from` each parked sender -> `run()` -> park (engine.rs:697-716). `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from` throws unless the source fragment has run. `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` returns a receiver only when every expected sender is complete. The remote path is also park-then-export (`EngineRequest::ExportNext`, engine.rs:91-95). Inside the engine, `Fragment::build()` opens a `StandaloneQueryScope` that takes the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`) until `run()` finishes, so two fragments cannot be in flight on one context even if the CN asked (source skeptic; this makes "run sender and receiver concurrently" engine work, not CN work).

**Measured, q05 timeline.** All 11 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs arrived 13:03:43.358-43.462 (cn1/cluster.log 4142-4202). Fragments ran strictly sequentially: nation 6 ms, region 9 ms, then the lineitem sender 5774 started 13:03:43.434 with `allocated=2304 bytes` (engine-cn0.log:49203, an empty pool) and parked 39 batches x 2.668 GB = 104.06 GB by +1.315 s (Quent data_batch Stationary events: 26.7 GB at +0.32 s, 66.7 GB at +0.88 s); first OOM at +1.361 s (engine-cn0.log:49221 `requested 748875880 bytes ... global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB), peak allocated 3376381184, reservation 3318948864`). The supplier/customer/orders fragments started only after the failure at 13:05:24.632+ (cluster.log 6072-6305); the receiver of streams 7 and 9 never started (Quent shows 7 of 11 fragments). Receiver 5775 later ran in 73 ms and its output sat parked for 184.5 s until q08's failure wipe (cn1-quent.txt wall=184.502 s, Comp=0.128 s).

**Measured, passing queries show the same shape under the cap.** cn1 q07.r0: all 7 senders finished before the join fragment started (cluster.log 6807-7005); 59.47 GB of lineitem plus 18.38 GB of orders were parked (79.1 GB, 74% of the pool) with dwell up to 2.76 s. cn4 q07.r1: every `fragment run finished` precedes its first `transmitted batches via nixl`. Per-fragment run sums vs span (MFS-4): cn1 q02.r1 13 fragments sum 977 ms, span 1067 ms, gaps 90 ms (8%); cn4 q02.r1 cn0 sum 748 ms, span 1081 ms, gaps 333 ms (31%), the largest before receivers waiting for the other CNs' senders. The 4-slot executor idles during the many 1-task fragments (cn1 q02.r1: 133 tasks, Comp 2.9 s in a 1.06 s span = 2.7 of 4 slots busy).

**Streaming works within a fragment.** q21 fragment 2acb (ran after the failure) streamed a 123 GB lineitem scan through FILTER -> HASH_JOIN in 3.15 s with only 46.47 GB partitioned out (cn1-quent.txt q21.r0). Only the exchange forces full materialisation.

**Proposed.** Two routes: (1) on 1 CN, fuse local-only fragments before translation (P1, item 2); every exchange is local, the fused plan is the standalone plan, no engine change. (2) Streaming receivers: build once build-side streams are complete, consume probe-side streams while the sender still runs, run sender and receiver concurrently. (2) requires per-fragment lifecycle/task creators in the engine (the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` and the shared `task_creator_` reset in `begin_execution_window`, `sirius_context.cpp:392-395`) and a build/probe decision before the streamed side's cardinality is known. Confidence high on the mechanism; medium (1) and low-medium (2) on design effort.

#### B2 (confirmed, mechanism sharpened). Parked batches are invisible to the downgrade sweep, so every OOM cycle frees 0 bytes although a 160 GiB HOST tier is configured

**Measured.** cn1/engine-cn0.log: 17,917 lines `[downgrade] [GPU:0] downgrade request not satisfied and disk memory space is not configured; data cannot be spilled to disk` and 17,917 `after downgrade (0 bytes freed), reservation still partial (...) -- proceeding with partial reservation`; per query 2503/3603/5603/2103/2302/1803. Zero lines with non-zero bytes freed. `[host_pool] HOST:0 ... allocated=72351744` is constant through the q05 storm (the host tier exists: `HOST_MEM=160GiB` -> `sirius.memory.host.capacity_bytes`, `engine_settings.rs:111-116`; `1 host memory space(s) created`). The bench kit already documents "host spill is NOT implemented" (`benchmarks/tpch/run-abc.sh:1038`).

**Source (verified).** `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`: `// Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment.` `_output_repos[id] = std::make_shared<cucascade::shared_data_repository>()` (and `_input_repos` likewise). The only registration path into a per-query manager is `repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-71 add_new_repository` (inter-pipeline ports). `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232` TIER 1 iterates `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` managers only; `:294-300` TIER 2 the pipeline task queue (queued GPU_SCAN tasks hold no input batches). The warning at `:357-363` fires whenever no DISK tier exists and the request is unsatisfied, regardless of whether any candidate existed. `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 output_row_count` throws on a non-GPU-resident parked batch (the CN swallows it with `.ok()` and plans blind, engine.rs:564, 582-585); `:822-825 export_packed` throws too, which would fail the 4-CN path on a spilled batch.

**Correction.** The original clause "the sender's engine query has already ended" is not the operative reason. In q05/q08/q09 the bytes that filled the pool (104.30/99.54/96.42 GB) are the *running* leaf fragment's own STREAMING_SINK output; its query and manager existed, but a `GPU_SCAN -> STREAMING_SINK` fragment registers no repository at all. Finished-sender outputs account for 0 / 4.7 / 8.8 GB in those three, 38.2 / 68.7 / 77.8 GB in q17/q18/q21. The escape from the manager is the whole mechanism, and the receiver's `_input_repos` are equally invisible.

**Impact arithmetic (inference).** Spilled data has to fit GPU + HOST = 107.4 + 171.8 = 279 GB. Totals a working spill would have to hold: q17 ~160 GB, q18 ~166, q05 ~171, q21 ~195, q08 ~200, q09 ~253. Five of six would plausibly pass slowly; q09 is marginal after the 16 GiB staging arena and the ~34 GB host-pool peak. The original "host spill rescues only q17/q18" compared against the host tier alone and should be dropped.

**Proposed.** Register the streaming sink's output repositories and the receiver's input repositories with a process-level registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, including the running fragment's own sink (otherwise q05/q08/q09 still die). Make `Fragment::output_row_count` read a row count from host metadata and `export_packed` accept HOST-tier batches (the local relay already upgrades HOST -> GPU in `lock_or_prepare_batch`). Correct the warning to distinguish "no convertible candidates" from "no disk tier". Note the newest-first fairness policy at `downgrade_executor.cpp:204-216`; the candidate that matters here is the newest fragment's own output. Confidence high on the mechanism, medium that spill is worth doing before P1/B1.

#### B3 (confirmed). The reschedule loop has no feasibility check: 179 stuck scan tasks x 100 retries x 50 ms, re-reading the split each time, while nothing can free memory

**Source (verified).** `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348 static constexpr uint32_t MAX_RETRIES = 100;` (comment: bumped from 10 for cross-GPU batch-lock contention), `:409 sleep_for(50ms)`, termination only by count (`:349-364`) or `_completion_handler->has_error()` (`:314`); `:263` proceeds with a partial reservation after 0 bytes freed. Each retry resumes at operator index 0 and re-runs `materialize_table` for the same split (`sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:530-533, 592-593`). No knob: `exec/config.hpp` has no retry field.

**Measured** (agent-notes/skeptic-oom4/retry_stats.py over cn1/engine-cn0.log):

| query | stuck tasks | reschedules | first OOM (from client start) | last reschedule | wall to die (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q05 | 25 | 2500 | +1.61 s | +101.33 s | 101.5 |
| q08 | 36 | 3600 | +1.73 | +168.15 | 168.3 |
| q09 | 56 | 5600 | +2.38 | +232.41 | 232.5 |
| q17 | 21 | 2100 | +1.20 | +103.74 | 103.9 |
| q18 | 23 | 2300 | +9.29 | +54.14 | 54.2 |
| q21 | 18 | 1800 | +2.68 | +114.23 | 114.5 |

Offsets are from the client start in `cn1/runs/runs.csv` (q05 13:03:43.185); B1's "+1.361 s" for q05 is the same first OOM (13:03:44.795) measured from the lineitem sender's start (13:03:43.434). Every original task reaches exactly retry 100; the retry chain of q05 task 2567 is byte-identical on all 101 attempts (requested 748,875,880 B, peak 3,376,381,184 B; the retry floor raised the request from 5.80 to 6.64 GB while the grant stayed at 3.08-3.32 GB = cap minus parked bytes). Quent q05 fragment 5774: `GPU_SCAN n=2543 Computing sum 229.5 s` (about half of it is the 50 ms sleep, which Quent counts inside Computing), `Queued 2228.6 s`, `Reserving 99.9 s`, for 40 useful batches that took 1.3 s. The storm is paced by the single manager thread blocking in `make_reservation` (Reserving sum equals the retry window: q05 99.9 s of 101.2), not by the sleeps. Exactly one successful task finalised after the first OOM in each of the six windows. The six failures consumed 774.9 s of the 910.3 s 1-CN sweep (85%). Log volume: 89,580 of 152,097 engine-log lines are the five per-retry lines. `SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS` cannot detect the storm because each reschedule creates and destroys a task, advancing the watchdog fingerprint (`sirius_engine.cpp:113-125`).

**Proposed.** At the reservation gate (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263`) abort the query when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry_reservation_floor > reservation->size()` (all three are local there), or in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and `global usage == usage_limit` and no successful completion happened since this task's previous attempt (`_tasks_executed` at `:310` is success-only). Keep the 100-retry budget for the contention case, which arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the reservation gate. Message the engine can emit: "104 GB parked by this fragment's sink, 3.1 GB grantable < 6.6 GB floor, downgrade freed 0 bytes". Effect: each failure dies in ~3 s (q18 ~10 s because its own senders run first). Confidence high; this is a robustness finding, no wrong result is produced.

#### B4 (disputed: mechanism confirmed, causal claim refuted). Fragments of a failed query keep running and park output nobody consumes; the leak is 0-38 GB per failure but decided no pass/fail here

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:449-476 cancel_plan_fragment` only calls `results.cancel()`; its log line reads `acknowledging cancel_plan_fragment (best-effort: no engine-side abort yet)` (:468) and the docstring says teardown "is a separate work item". `engine.rs:291-316` drops parked outputs only when `run_fragment` returns `Err`, and then wipes every slot process-wide. `ResultStore.query_failures` (result_store.rs:98) is recorded but never consulted on the sender path. A translator failure before the run (q16) drops the `LocalParked` slots without `drop_parked`.

**Measured** (engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] allocated` at fragment boundaries, agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt `base@start`): after q05 4.69 GB carried through q06/q07; after q08 8.83 GB into q09; after q09 31.56 GB through q10..q16 (seven queries); +6.6 GB from q16's parked partsupp scan -> 38.16 GB at q17's start; after q17 4.0 GB into q18; after q18 0; after q21 36.64 GB into q22 (q22 cold 4110 ms vs 943 warm). cluster.log shows the dead query's queued senders starting after `fragment run failed` (q05: 5773, 5777, 5776, 5775 at 13:05:24.632+, the first 0.25 ms before the FE's first cancel ack). Engine-thread time stolen from the next query: q17 -> q18 6.42 s, q21 -> q22 ~3.35 s, q08 -> q09 1.04 s.

**Objection (both skeptics).** "Directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false: q17's F00 lineitem projection is ~120-122 GB (46 tasks x 2.65 GB; standalone `GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB`), above the 107.37 GB cap, so it fails with zero leak; the leak only moved the death from ~40 to 25 parked batches. Every passing query that ran under a leak passed with `oom_resched=0` (q06/q07 under 4.69 GB, q10-q15 under 31.6-38.2 GB, q22 under 36.6 GB). No pass/fail in this campaign was decided by the leak. The order-dependence risk is real but inferred: q07's own parked footprint is 79.17 GB; under the 38.16 GB leak it would need ~117 GB and would have failed had it run between q09 and q17. The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).

**Proposed (small, high confidence as hygiene).** Store `query_id` with each `ParkedOutput`; on `Err` drop only that query's slots; keep a failed-query set on the engine thread and skip its pending `Run`s (Err-time bookkeeping, since cancel arrives after the next sender already started); make `cancel_plan_fragment` drop the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeue its fragments (needs a `LocalExchange` removal by query; today removals happen only in `take_ready`, local_exchange.rs:284-308); in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm `drop_parked` the slots already in hand when translation fails.

#### B5 (confirmed, proposals corrected). Shuffle drains are serialised after the fragment finishes, and 84-88% of each drain is `export_packed` on the engine thread at ~63 GB/s

**Measured, cn4 q03.r1** (cn4/cluster.log): each lineitem sender finished at +0.610..0.684 s, then performed 3 sequential transmits of 4.82-4.89 GB, each `elapsed_ms=92-98 lease_ms=1-2 write_ms=6-8` (600-717 GB/s write), completing at +95/+190/+283 ms after finish; the next fragment on that CN (customer scan) started 0.1-0.3 ms after the last transmit on all 4 CNs. Same pattern in q03.r0/r2 and in q10.r1 (lineitem 0.145-0.159 s, customer 0.083-0.102 s), q12.r1 (0.115-0.125 s), q19.r1 (0.055-0.078 s). The Quent staging-lease probe times the pack directly: 48-52 sender-side leases per CN of ~311 MB, pack median 4.9 ms per lease = 63.5 GB/s, non-pack (lease RPC + write + transmit RPC) 0.7 ms, so pack = 84-88% of the drain for q03 (74-82% q10/q12, 18-32% q19 with 7 MB batches). Receiver-side unpack of the same frames: 0.14 ms per 303 MB (2.1 TB/s), ~30x faster than the pack.

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:1207-1219` comment: "one FIFO request channel into ONE transport thread ... the drains still run one at a time, in the FE's destination order"; `:380-392 dispatch_worker` is one thread; `:864-872 run_ready_fragment ... .and_then(FragmentOutcome::join_into_ready)` joins the drains before yielding; `nixl_transport.rs:713-775` drain loop (`export_packed_next` per batch, lease RPC, `write_and_wait`, transmit RPC); `engine.rs:813 export_packed_next = engine_call` served by the single engine thread (engine.rs:321-324); `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:~800 kPackChunkBytes = 8 MiB` with `cudf::chunked_pack` on the default stream (~37 `next()` launches per 311 MB batch). The serialisation on the dispatch worker exists because `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` was set (capture-cn.sh:12; default off); with the default, the same drain holds the RPC open and delays the FE's next deploy stage instead (`Deployer.java:236-243, 318`). Either way it is on the critical path.

**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.

**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.

#### B6 (confirmed). The staging arena is 87-88% full for q03 and q07 at 4 CNs, and exhaustion fails the query instead of applying backpressure

**Measured.** cn4 q03.r1 receiver on 9102: stream 2 frames 4.8885 + 4.8423 + 4.8506 GB + 3 x 0.146 (stream 9) + 3 x 0.03 (stream 6) = 15.1 GB = 14.1 GiB of the 16 GiB arena (cn4/cluster.log `received remote batches`); Quent whole-query occupancy peak 14.95-15.10 GB of 17.18 GB per CN at +1.28 s. Frames land at +0.71..+1.01 s and are consumed at +1.30 s (dwell 0.4-0.6 s while the customer and orders x customer fragments run and the receiver waits for all four senders). q07.r1: lineitem 3 x 3.62-3.68 + orders 3 x 1.13 + customer 3 x 0.30 = ~15.2 GB per CN. q10 6.4-11.7 GiB, q12 5.4-6.0, q14 <= 3.3, q19 0.7. Lease waits are zero (cn4-transmits.txt `lease_ms` median 0, max 15 ms in q12.r1), which is consistent with a non-blocking arena, not with "no pressure". Peak lease concurrency per CN: q07.r1 63-64, q03.r1 55-56 (cn4-quent.txt per-fragment `maxconc`; session-wide max 94, WORKFLOW-PLAN fact 13) against no lease-count limit, so the arena is bounded by bytes only; per-query lease counts and GB in cn4-quent.txt are time-attributed and can bleed into the next run (tooling defect AGG-6 below), which is why per-stream bytes above come from cn4/cluster.log rather than from the lease digest.

**Source (verified).** `src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248` throws `exchange staging arena exhausted: requested {} bytes ... (raise SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES)`; `nixl_transport.rs:720 rpc_request_lease(...)?` propagates the error out of the drain; `compute_node_service.rs:1302 handle_staging_lease` has no wait or retry. The arena's own destructor summary never printed because the CNs were force-exited.

**Impact (inference, medium).** With the current FE plan the arena requirement for q03 grows as lineitem/N: ~SF1150 with `STAGING=16GiB`, or SF1000 with a 12 GiB arena, fails q03 after all the scan work is done. Broadcasting the small side (P3) would need < 1 GB of arena per CN for this family.

**Proposed.** Short term: document `STAGING >= (N-1)/N x largest shuffled stream` in the cn-tuning guidance and fix P3. Engine: make `exchange_staging_arena::lease` block with a bounded wait on release instead of throwing, so a full arena throttles senders; or let the receiver push remote frames into pool memory on arrival (`push_packed` is already a deep copy) and release the lease immediately, keeping only the per-frame row count for `declare_input_cardinality`. Confidence high on the occupancy and the failure path.

#### B7 (medium confidence, not adversarially verified). Per-task GPU_SCAN time rises 1.3-1.6x when four CNs scan concurrently, and at 1 CN the 4 pipeline slots bound the scan

**Measured.** Per-task GPU_SCAN Computing (ms per ~2.2-2.3 GB task, `*-quent.json top_ops`): q03 lineitem 102 (1 CN) / 134-145 (4 CN) / 111 (standalone); q10 90 / 100-119 / 96; q12 orders 107 / 131-146 / 117; q14 151 / 240-249 / 176; q19 85 / 113-126 / 98; q07 130 / 179-186 / 142; q06 100 / 138-146. Per GB: q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q13 0.322 -> 0.498. q01 additionally shows 0.5-0.87 s stalls on 10% of splits on 2-3 of the 4 CNs, varying per run, with balanced bytes per CN (agent-notes/agg-only.md section 4); the 4-CN scan fragment is 1.43x (q01) / 1.6x (q06) the ideal quarter of the 1-CN fragment, which is 26-31% of the 4-CN wall. Aggregate read rates: q01 8.2 GB/s (1 CN) vs 22.9 GB/s (4 CN); q06 20.5 vs 50.8 GB/s, so the storage has headroom over what 4 slots pull. At 1 CN all 107 (q01) / 65 (q06) scan tasks are created within 9-50 ms and the 4 slots are busy 98%+ of the fragment wall (Queued median = half the wall); the memory gate does not bind for these two.

**Cause not identified.** The `scan_split_read` probe recorded counts only in the digest because `quent_bp.py` reads the wrong attribute keys (`bytes`/`elapsed_ns` instead of `compressed_bytes`/`output_bytes`/`materialize_ns` emitted by `src/telemetry/scan_telemetry.cpp:52-56`), and even the raw probe covers read + decode together (`materialize_ns`). Candidates: GPFS client contention on concurrent O_DIRECT streams from 16 slots, host/GPU-side effects, NUMA placement. The CN launcher cannot raise `pipeline.num_threads` because `engine_settings.rs::derive_sirius_config_yaml` emits no pipeline block (and pairs with C3: 8 slots would request 156 GB in the cold-start wave).

**Proposed.** Split the probe into read and decode, fix the digest keys (AGG-6), then A/B `SIRIUS_CN_USE_SIRIUS_DATASOURCE=false` and buffered reads / prefetch cache with the page cache warm vs dropped; add `SIRIUS_CN_PIPELINE_THREADS` to the derived config and sweep 6 and 8 on 1 CN with Quent on.

#### Disputed backpressure finding

**BJ-6: "memory backpressure is absent for q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 at both 1 and 4 CN; the 6-15x over-reservation is harmless because concurrent reservations are far below the pool": refuted on the 1-CN half and on the mechanism; the conclusion (memory pressure is not this family's loss) stands.** Objection (data skeptic, agent-notes/refute-bj6): 4 concurrent tasks hold 58-80% of the 107.37 GB limit, not "far below"; the reservation gate blocked 47-178 ms per run in q10/q12/q14 at 1 CN in all three runs (see C3), 0 at 4 CNs and standalone; the engine pool's running peak reached 92-99% of the limit inside q03.r0 and q04.r0. "No arena exhaustion" is vacuous evidence because exhaustion is a hard failure, never backpressure (B6). The proposed regression guard is inverted: a tighter estimate reduces gating; guard instead that `num_threads x per-task cold-start request` stays well under the limit. Cost today is <= 0.18 s per query, so the impact ranking (planning, CN serialisation, scan contention dominate) survives.

#### Tooling defects found on the way (AGG-6, high confidence)

`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:98-104` attributes staging leases by a +-0.5 s time window, so the last run of each query inherits the next cold run's first leases (cn4 q06.r2 shows 55 leases / 25.6 GB although q06 moves 64 bytes per stream; cn4-quent.txt per-fragment lease counts are likewise attributed by time, e.g. q07.r1's 1-task nation fragment shows 184 leases). Use cn4-cnlog.json per-stream transmit bytes for volume. `quent_bp.py:60-70 scan_reads` uses the wrong keys (see B7). Fix both before the next capture.

---

## 4. What to do first

Costs: 3 proto messages, ~600 lines + tests, new FE class, cost-model patch, 5 SET GLOBALs; broadcast_row_limit=2e9 also relaxes PushDownAggregateCollector.java:647; rows_ranges may regress q10 (its own table); q09 prediction is weak (partsupp 800M and orders 1.5e9 unfiltered builds would be broadcast/parked, ~34 GB). Internal inconsistency: summary lists q18 among the five that pass, section 4 case A says q18 needs item 5. Citation error: l_commitdate < l_receiptdate is 0.5 (BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.java:369-374), not 0.8 (:615-616 is the NE path). Omits the CI patch-apply step (.github/workflows/experimental.yml:52-57 applies only nixl-exchange-proto.patch by name) so the CN CI build would fail on the new proto field.

input.winner: upstream (files-cardinality-upstream.md), with the robust design's Part B split off as a separate gate-decided follow-up
input.reasoning: Measured facts (re-checked in the worktree at 45dab3be): every FILES() scan is planned at 1 row (StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676, reached from :374-376); the physical FILES() operator falls through to visitOperator (OperatorVisitor.java:454-456) but is never re-derived in the main path (extractBestPlan copies group statistics, QueryOptimizer.java:1112; PlanFragmentBuilder.java:4294 uses optExpression.getStatistics()), so the visitPhysicalTableFunctionTableScan override in robust/upstream is harmless and defensive. All three designs remove the 1-row default; only upstream and robust make the leaf counts exact (parquet footers the CN already parses, file_schema.rs:19-25; parquet 59.2.0 per Cargo.lock:1648). The surgical estimator under-counts lineitem 4.9x and inverts partsupp/orders and part/customer; those biases enter S_L in every HashJoinCostModel comparison, which is what the whole fix is for. Inference (hand computation from CostModel.java:129-135/419-441, HashJoinCostModel.java:86-156, EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-327, all verified): with real counts and stock settings the FE still hash-partitions lineitem at 1 CN for the six (broadcast probe penalty up to 12 vs shuffle cap 3; x1000 above exec_mem_limit 2 GiB; single-node shuffle network cost 0 when enable_local_shuffle_agg is true) and additionally flips q03 (78 GB of lineitem) and q12 (36 GB of orders) from streaming to parking at 1 CN. So surgical and upstream 'fix' C1 (cardinalities) but not the six, and can break two of the 15 passing queries on 1 CN if enabled by default without settings; both say so and gate with a mutable Config plus an EXPLAIN COSTS survey. Robust is the only design that would move lineitem to the streamed probe side, but only through a coupled bundle (exec_mem_limit 64 GiB, enable_local_shuffle_agg=false, broadcast_row_limit 2e9, cbo_cte_reuse=false, plus a flag-gated cap in HashJoinCostModel.getAvgProbeCost); I confirmed its q05/q03/q12 signs with the verified constants and that exec_mem_limit is FE-only in this deployment (the CN never reads TQueryOptions.mem_limit). That bundle is fix 4(d) of the plan, not fix 3: it changes every distribution decision in the cluster, is hand-computed with two coin flips (f, pf), risks q10 at 4 CN in its default mode, and comes with ~600 lines, three proto messages, a new FE class, a missing CI step and an internal inconsistency on q18. Correctness/cancellation: all three are planning-only on the FE plus a larger reply payload on an RPC whose wait is already unbounded (TableFunctionTable.java:713); no CN execution path, cancel path or result path changes; the CN executes whatever fragment shape arrives and fails closed by name on RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN (node_translator.rs:1743-1762) and MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK (compute_node_service.rs:1519), which all three flag with the right mitigations (plan item 5 first; SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse=false, effective via CTEContext.needInline:157-190 and cbo_cte_max_limit=10 > 8 CTEs). Acceptance tests: upstream's are the soundest (fake:// UTs for the fallback at 153 rows, MockUp for the footer path, CN fixture tests summing row groups, EXPLAIN goldens on a clean 1-CN cluster, which matters because the survey had 4 CN ids registered so isSingleBackendAndComputeNode was false); surgical's golden as written ('estimate before predicates') does not match what EXPLAIN COSTS prints for FileScanNodes with conjuncts; robust's is a larger matrix (2 modes x 2 node counts) whose SF1000 pass criterion depends on five settings. Totals tie surgical and upstream at 19; the tie goes to upstream because exact counts are the deliverable of issue 3, PR-A of upstream is the surgical design (nothing is lost), the extra surface is one optional proto2 field and ~40 lines of Rust with zero extra I/O, and it is the only one that already handles the CI patch-apply step and the clean-cluster caveat.
input.merge_suggestions: Take upstream as the base (PR-A FE patch with fallback + knob, PR-B optional num_rows + CN + CI generalisation). Merge from surgical: the explicit isListFilesOnly() guard (TableFunctionTable.java:432; do not rely on fileStatuses being empty), the mutable-knob A/B procedure on one FE, SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse=false in the bench bring-up (bench.sh:85 today only defines MYSQL), and its per-query prediction table (section 3.3) as the checklist for diffing plan-summary goldens; fix its golden wording to post-predicate FileScanNode cardinalities. Merge from robust: (1) set tableRowCountMayInaccurate(true) only on the bytes/width fallback path (exact path false), (2) the one-line FE INFO per statement (path, files, rows, source=footer|estimated) and the CN get_file_schema span fields files/rows, (3) the PlanTestBase test with injected statistics asserting join side and distribution (stronger than a contains-assert on 'cardinality: 153'), (4) the build.rs guard extension for the new proto token, (5) its Part B as a separate, flag-gated 'fix 3b' decided at the EXPLAIN COSTS gate: conf/sirius-cbo-defaults.sql with cbo_cte_reuse=false now, and exec_mem_limit / enable_local_shuffle_agg=false / broadcast_row_limit plus the enable_sirius_gpu_join_cost probe-penalty cap only after the 1-CN EXPLAIN survey shows the q03/q12 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flips it is meant to prevent; this is the plan's fix 4(d) and should be scheduled next to fix 4a, with item 5 (translator RIGHT_SEMI) landing first. Do not merge robust's per-file PFileStatistics or per-column min/max yet: no decision examined changes sign between the 0.25 default and the footer range (q05 orders 0.152 vs 0.25), so ranges add proto/CN/FE surface without a measured payoff; keep the single optional int64 num_rows = 3 and revisit ranges if the gate shows a range-driven decision. Fix upstream's string-equality note (1.0, not 0.5) before it becomes a golden.
disqualifiers: None of the three is disqualified outright; the following are 'cannot work as written' items that must be fixed before implementation.

robust: the CN change adds fields to PGetFileSchemaResult but the design's file list omits .github/workflows/experimental.yml (:52-57 applies only patches/nixl-exchange-proto.patch by name), so the CN CI build fails to compile the new struct fields; one-line fix (apply scripts/apply-starrocks-patches.sh) that the upstream design already includes.

robust: internal contradiction on q18 (summary: passes with Part A+B; section 4 case A: needs plan item 5 for the LEFT SEMI commutation) and a wrong citation for l_commitdate < l_receiptdate (0.5 via BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.java:369-374, not 0.8 via :615-616 which is the NE path); numbers off by 1.6x on q04's build, sign unchanged.

surgical: acceptance test A's golden ('each FileScanNode prints the section 2.3 estimate before predicates') does not match EXPLAIN COSTS, which prints the post-conjunct row count on the FileScanNode (visitOperator applies the scan predicate, StatisticsCalculator.java:245-300; survey/explain/q05.costs.txt:334-342 shows the o_orderdate range on FileScanNode 2); the goldens must be post-predicate values (e.g. orders 1.42e8 not 5.69e8) or the test must assert on the table-level estimate.

surgical: width uses getFullSchema(), which includes columns_from_path STRING columns (TableFunctionTable.java:270-271); harmless for the TPC-H bench, wrong in general (upstream's getFileColumns() excludes them).

upstream: the 'correction' that string equality on an UNKNOWN column is 0.5 is wrong; StatisticRangeValues.overlapPercentWith (:84-89) returns min(1/1,1)=1.0 for an infinite intersect with both ndv finite, and convertStatisticsToDouble returns empty for CHAR/VARCHAR (StatisticUtils.java:457-459), so the report's C1 (1.0) stands; its worked numbers for o_orderstatus='F' (750M) and c_mktsegment should be 1.5e9 / 1.5e8, no sign change in its cost tables.

surgical and upstream (shared, not a design error but a deployment hazard): with the knob on by default at 1 CN, both designs' own arithmetic (confirmed here) predicts q03 parks ~78 GB of lineitem and q12 ~36 GB of orders in the 100 GiB pool; neither may be enabled for a 1-CN SF1000 arm before the EXPLAIN COSTS survey on a clean single-node FE (the survey cluster had CN ids 10001/11001/12002/12003 registered, so isSingleBackendAndComputeNode was false and shuffle network cost was counted; a clean 1-CN FE zeroes it and makes shuffles cheaper still).
